answer: One enforceable rule: require consistent long-form persona presence across two disconnected communities. Clustering on shared timing signatures exposes the operator. Because it works by raising the marginal cost per fabricated identity to roughly a full epoch of compute, cluster rewards are paid once, not per address. The inlet of work and the basalt of evidence must both recur for the same identity, and a spiral to an external peer is the only path that releases the bond.
